Reference [9] states the army went from employing '3 million people' to 100,000, implying 2.9 million job losses. However, this is historically inaccurate—the pre-treaty German army was not a standing force of 3 million civilians employed in the military. The peacetime army before WWI was around 700,000; demobilization after 1918 already reduced it drastically. The response and its sources exaggerate the economic impact of military downsizing by citing implausible employment figures, creating a misleading causal link.
